description: One question per line of a research brief, each naming a single way a line can be wrong. The brief's line goes in the segment; the sources it cites belong in the state's input field.

figure-differs-from-source.instructions: This line gives a figure that differs from the figure in the source it cites.

criteria.true: The number in the line does not match the number in the cited source.
criteria.false: The number matches the cited source, no number appears in the line.

claim-unsupported-by-citation.instructions: This line makes a claim that the source behind its bracketed marker does not support.

criteria.true: The cited source says nothing that establishes the claim.
criteria.false: The cited source establishes the claim.

undated-source-as-current.instructions: This line presents an undated source as current.

criteria.true: The line implies recency for a source whose date is unknown.
criteria.false: The line carries a date, the line makes no claim about recency.

secondhand-as-first-party.instructions: This line presents a statistic taken from elsewhere as the citing publication's own.

criteria.true: The publication named in the line only repeated the figure from another publication.
criteria.false: The publication named in the line produced the figure itself.

population-mismatch.instructions: This line describes a population that differs from the population the cited study measured.

criteria.true: The group in the line is not the group the study sampled.
criteria.false: The group in the line is the group the study sampled.

collector-mismatch.instructions: This line names a collector of the data that differs from the one the source names.

criteria.true: The line credits the wrong organisation with gathering the data.
criteria.false: The line credits the organisation the source credits.

vendor-claim-as-fact.instructions: This line states a vendor's claim about its own product as established fact.

criteria.true: A marketing claim by the seller is repeated without attribution to the seller.
criteria.false: The line attributes the claim to the seller, the claim comes from an independent source.

year-not-in-source.instructions: This line gives a year that the cited source does not state.

criteria.true: The year in the line appears nowhere in the source.
criteria.false: The year in the line comes from the source, no year appears.

currently-not-in-source.instructions: This line calls something current when the cited source says nothing about the present.

criteria.true: A present-tense framing is added that the source does not carry.
criteria.false: The source itself establishes the present-tense framing.

author-domain-mismatch.instructions: This line names an organisation as the author while its bracketed marker points at another domain.

criteria.true: The named author does not own the domain behind the marker.
criteria.false: The named author owns the domain behind the marker.

workers-stated-as-businesses.instructions: This line reports a survey of workers as a share of businesses.

criteria.true: The unit measured was people, the line reports companies.
criteria.false: The unit in the line matches the unit measured.

general-advice-as-ai-advice.instructions: This line recasts general advice as advice specific to AI.

criteria.true: The cited guidance was not about AI at all.
criteria.false: The cited guidance was about AI.

one-price-as-general.instructions: This line states the price of one product as true of the category.

criteria.true: A single vendor's price is presented as what such tools cost.
criteria.false: The line attributes the price to the one product.

sample-size-missing.instructions: This line reports a survey result whose sample size it does not give.

criteria.true: A survey finding appears with no indication of how many were asked.
criteria.false: The sample size appears, the line reports no survey finding.

projection-as-measurement.instructions: This line presents a projection as a measured result.

criteria.true: A forecast is written in the past tense, a forecast is written as an observation.
criteria.false: The line marks the figure as a forecast.

correlation-as-cause.instructions: This line presents a correlation as a cause.

criteria.true: The source reports an association, the line asserts causation.
criteria.false: The line keeps the association an association.

global-figure-as-local.instructions: This line applies a worldwide figure to one country.

criteria.true: A global statistic is written as though it described a single market.
criteria.false: The scope in the line matches the scope of the figure.

superlative-unsupported.instructions: This line uses a superlative that no cited source establishes.

criteria.true: A claim of most, best, fastest, largest rests on nothing in the sources.
criteria.false: The superlative comes from a source, no superlative appears.

paraphrase-changes-meaning.instructions: This line paraphrases its source in a way that changes what the source means.

criteria.true: A reader of the source would object to the paraphrase.
criteria.false: The paraphrase preserves the source's meaning.

definition-invented.instructions: This line defines a term in a way no cited source gives.

criteria.true: The definition appears nowhere in the sources.
criteria.false: The definition comes from a source, the line defines nothing.

marketing-page-as-evidence.instructions: This line treats a marketing page as independent evidence.

criteria.true: The cited page exists to sell the thing it is cited about.
criteria.false: The cited page is independent of what it establishes.
